- When sentiment is predominantly negative (≥ 3 consecutive -1.00), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for 2–4 days.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive (e.g., -1 → 1), model underreacts; increase forecast by 3–7% for next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes when sentiment is mixed or neutral (e.g., 1.00/ -1.00 alternating); apply 5–10% upward bias for 5–7 days.
- If true outcome exceeds model by >10% for 2+ consecutive days, assume mean reversion; reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags true trend by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to align with 3-day moving average of true outcomes if sentiment is stable.
- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 3 consecutive 1.00), model tends to overfit upward trend; cap forecast at 5–8% below 30-day high for 3–5 days.
